questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Reflecting on my recent exchange experience in Zürich, several factors were instrumental in my decision to choose this destination for my studies. Foremost among these was the exceptional academic reputation of both the University of Zürich and ETH Zürich. These institutions are renowned for their rigorous academic standards and pioneering research, which aligned perfectly with my educational aspirations. Additionally, Switzerland's breathtaking landscapes offered endless opportunities for hiking and outdoor adventures, providing a much-needed balance to my academic pursuits. Moreover, I found Switzerland's culture to be surprisingly reminiscent of Denmark's, which brought a comforting sense of familiarity to my experience abroad. This cultural similarity made the transition smoother and enriched my stay, making it an invaluable part of my academic and personal growth.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus is quite manageable. Many accommodations consist of dormitory rooms that foster a vibrant social atmosphere, effectively compensating for the campus social life you might miss out on. This setup provides a unique opportunity to engage with a diverse group of students and can significantly enhance your overall exchange experience.

questions.answer: One is able to try out several courses the first two weeks and choose the courses one find interesting and then deregister from the rest. Very smart system!

questions.answer: It was all online in the students platform OLAT

questions.answer: MA

questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was the same as my home university (University of Copenhagen) but there are a lot of 3 ECTS point courses, and then one end up with a lot of courses. The students from Zürich are not commonly taking 30 credits each semester, but this was not told to us. Therefore we had a lot of studying compared to the local students.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much the same.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Enroll as a special student in ETH and choose some of their courses. They have very good courses in Energy economics.

Applied Time Series with R was an applied course, which was good to try on real life data and not just learn theory. 
Labor economics: the professor is really good and overall exciting course.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. They are very private people as Danes are, but the exchange students are more open and willing to get to know new people.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Find other exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any. They are pretty private.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are very organised.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find other exchange students. It's good socially and you can help one another with all the pratical stuff.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find other exchange students. It's good socially and you can help one another with all the pratical stuff.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The social aspect. Getting to know many different people from your own country and from other countries.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: All the practical stuff in the beginning.
